title: Token Economy Simulator & Safeguard Hub for Batching/Caching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact interactive panel inside the Redwood Console that helps engineers explore token-level cost/latency trade-offs for different batching and caching configurations and compose safety guardrails. Two main pieces: (1) Token Economy Simulator — a live visualizer that simulates request flows, token counts, KV cache hits/misses, estimated cost and p50/p95 latency under a chosen policy; (2) Safeguard Hub — a lightweight policy composer for guardrails (max tokens per request, early-stop rules, model-fallback tiers, prefix-cache whitelist) with explainers and runtime impact preview.
background: Customers frequently ask for clearer, actionable guidance on how batching and caching settings translate to real cost and latency. Existing recommendation cards are static and lack a quick way to compare policies side-by-side or to author safe defaults. Ops teams need guardrails they can trust while developers want to experiment without risking large bill spikes. This ticket consolidates simulation, recommendation, and policy composition into one contextual UX inside the route and model settings pages.
goals: Make the impact of batching/caching settings immediately visible (cost, latency, cache hit rate)
Provide prescriptive, ranked recommendations for common workload patterns (chat, embeddings, rerank)
Allow safe composition of guardrails with previewed runtime consequences
Ship an accessible, mobile-friendly prototype for PM and Eng review
user_stories: As an engineer, I want to simulate 1k requests with my current batch size to see projected cost and 95th percentile latency so I can set safe defaults.
As a platform operator, I want to define a fallback chain (cheap quantized model -> default -> premium model) with automatic thresholds so we maintain uptime under load.
As a PM, I want the console to surface recommended presets for each workload type so teams can adopt best-practices quickly.
research_findings: From interviews with 7 internal customers: lack of quick feedback loop causes conservative presets and overprovisioning.
Support tickets show common mistakes: misconfigured prefix cache TTL and too-large max batch resulting in latency spikes.
Quantization recommendations need a confidence score and fallback plan before being shown as 'safe'.
design_decisions: Inline simulator sits in a collapsible drawer in model-route settings to keep surface area small.
Use three summary KPIs (cost per 1k requests, p50 latency, cache hit rate) plus a small sparkline for distribution.
Recommendations are ranked by estimated ROI and labeled with risk level (safe | moderate | aggressive).
Guardrails are stored as named policies so they can be reused across routes and exported/imported.
Preview mode will run only client-side estimates; actual rollout will require a runtime evaluation job triggered by backend (ENG dependency).
tradeoffs: Estimator accuracy vs. speed: a fast, client-side estimator gives immediate feedback but sacrifices fidelity for complex KV cache behavior.
Complex policy composer increases cognitive load; decided to hide advanced options behind "Learn more" and an "Advanced" toggle.
Exposing cost estimates risks overconfidence — added confidence bands and clear microcopy explaining variance.
